review:paths.verdict: Outside the width fold, I found no JIT miscompile, no wrong interpreter value, no wrong blame and no wrong guard-exit behaviour. There is one concrete divergence from 5.3.6, in the string reader of the slow path, plus one doc gap in U9. Recorder: the EQ round-trip guard, the record-time decisions for constant counts (63, 64, 65, -1, -63, -64, -2^63, 2^62, and ~>> case by case), the CONV int.num CHECK + ULT 64 guard for variable counts, int operands sign-extended, strings aborting, and the result CONV num.i64 all behave as designed [S oclj_bitop_rec.c:28-101; IR shape seen in -jdump]. Exact-iteration check: fresh loops, with the bad element placed at iterations 2..300 including the recording iteration itself. The bad values were 1.5, NaN, ±2^63, 2^64, ±inf, -0.0, a denormal, numeric and non-numeric strings, table, boolean, and counts of 64/65/-1/-64/2^31/2^32/±0.5/1.5/-2^63. On all 25200 cases the prototype raised the same error, at the same iteration, naming the same local, as PUC 5.3.6, and computed the same values. JIT on, -joff and -Ohotloop=1 were identical, and 41400 more cases with ~>> were identical between JIT and -joff [M]. The un-stubbed int64 folds (kfold_int64arith/shift/bnot, simplify_andor_k64, reassoc_intarith_k64, simplify_shiftk_andk, plus the generic band/bor/bxor/shift rules on KINT64) give PUC's values in loops built to fire them [M]. A class-switching random differential found 0 differences across 3000 programs, and also under 11 option sets (-O0, -O1, -O-fold, -O-cse, -O-narrow, -O-loop, -O-fuse, -O-sink, -O-fwd -O-dse, -Omaxside=0, -O3 -Ohotloop=1 -Ohotexit=1) [M]. Interpreter fast path [S vm_x64.dasc:1098-1135, 3527-3600]: NaN leaves via jp; 2^63 and above leave via jne; -2^63 and -0.0 are accepted; the shift count is checked with an unsigned cmp 63; ->vmeta_bitop_pc reloads RC/RA from PC_RB/PC_RC; BNOT passes its operand as both rb and rc. The 54 naming cases match 5.3.6 apart from the known 'field ?' residual [M]. Parser: on 9640 literal cases, folded equals run-time, and against PUC only the known inherent classes differ [M]. Folding works through const locals without changing the constant, and compound assignment is correct [M]. 139 strings x 9 operations agree with PUC except two strings, and both come from the one finding: ob_str2d inherits lj_strscan's 2^20 exponent limit [M].

review:tablefold.verdict: The extra fold works and is safe, but it recovers only about a quarter of the slowdown. It turns CONV int.num(CONV num.i64 y) into the unguarded CONV int.i64 y when oclj_bitwidth(y) <= 32, and does not fold across a PHI. All builds ran in one session, best of 3. Table CRC32 drops from 14.10 to 10.85 ns/byte with N=2e7, against 2.90 for today's build (b0) and 37.75 for PUC 5.3.6. The bench_bit2 run with N=5e7 gives 12.28 for the prototype (b1, whose three runs were 12.34, 12.28 and 14.12) and 10.88 for my variant. So the variant is still 3.7x slower than b0 [M]. The other loops are unchanged against b1: bit-serial CRC 90.9 against 91.35, the shl/xor/and loop 0.39 against 0.40, RGB 3.78 against 3.80 [M]. The variant passes everything with zero JIT-against-interpreter differences, and every output matches b1's file for file: t_jit2 (default, -joff, -O3 -Ohotloop=1), t_rec seeds 1 and 2 in normal and counts modes, t_sar (no SPLIT, equal to the model), the 7440-case t_ops, and the fuzzer at SEED=1 CASES=1000 (PASS, all four controls behave) [M]. The existing suites cannot see this fold: a sabotage build that folds at width <= 33 passes all of them, fuzzer included. Only my new t_idx.lua catches it, with 21 differing cases [M]. The design's diagnosis is half right. (a) is real: the guarded CONV int.num of the masked index is on the dependency chain, and removing it saves about 3.2 ns/byte. (b) is not the main cost: the checked round trip of each table-loaded value runs alongside the chain, not on it (only its cvttsd2si is on it, and any conversion needs one). The real cost is the rounding round trips that sit on the loop-carried chain: crc is carried as a double PHI, (crc ~ byte) is rounded before & 0xff, and crc >> 8 has a 57-bit bound. They exist because crc's width is unknown, which comes from the table values and from crc's starting value in a stack slot. For (b) I measured an int64-domain range guard as an experiment. It guards (y>>53)+1 <= 1 unsigned and then uses y directly instead of the round trip. Emitted only in loop bodies (variant rg2), it brings table CRC to 3.55 ns/byte (1.22x b0), passes every suite, and has no slowdown on loops whose values exceed 2^53 (24.1 against 23.8 ns/it). Emitted everywhere (variant rg), it slows the shl/xor/and loop by 1.3x and makes values above 2^53 7-18x slower. A version fit to ship needs more than a small change, so I describe it rather than recommend it for round 3.

review:widthfold.verdict:
I could not break the width fold, and I believe it is sound. The argument I accept is the main session's sharper one, made precise. [S] oclj_bitwidth (build copy lj_opt_fold.c:1159-1207) depends only on three things in the DAG below a ref: opcodes, IR types, and constants (KINT64 values and KINT shift counts). It never reads a runtime value. Every way a loop-carried double reaches an int64 op is a num-to-i64 CONV, and that CONV gets bound 64 (:1168-1171). This covers SLOADs, table and upvalue loads that the loop copy forwards, and parent SLOADs in side traces. I checked each rule against every value its operands can take, and each is a correct interval bound:
- KINT64: kwidth.
- int-typed ref: 33, which covers both sign and zero extension.
- CONV from int: 32 for SEXT, 33 otherwise.
- BAND with a non-negative constant: that constant's width; with the constant as op1 it falls through to max, which is still sound.
- BOR/BXOR: max. BNOT: unchanged.
- ADD: max+1 (only `x << 1` produces an int64 ADD).
- BSHL by a constant: +k, capped at 64.
- BSHR by a constant k of 1 or more: 65-k.
- BSAR by a constant: -k, floored at 1.
- Counts are taken & 63, which matches simplify_shift_ik and asm_bitshift. A KINT64 count gets 64.

[S] Types are iteration-invariant: loop_unroll converts or raises TYPEINS (lj_opt_loop.c:343-352). Constants are the same in every copy. A loop-copy instruction computes the same operator on the copies of its operands, and folds and CSE preserve values under LuaJIT's PHI semantics. By induction over the pre-roll DAG, the bound computed from a pre-roll instruction's tree therefore bounds that instruction's value in every iteration. That is exactly the set of values its PHI register carries. Snapshots only ever hold the num CONV, and it is exact when the bound is 54 or less, so restoring the carried double on exit is exact. The design's §3.5 step 3 ("bound at most the pre-roll's") is not what the code relies on.

[M] Empirical results:
- My generator (C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r3/review/widthfold/gen/gen.lua, drv.lua, sweep.sh) produced 120000 adversarial loops. They mix slot, table and upvalue feedback, branches, a flipped boolean, inner loops, an inlined helper, string.byte, int-typed results, stitching, five loop-header shapes, double arithmetic on the same variables, and counts and masks clustered at the bound.
- Each loop ran from 7 starts, with shared and fresh closures, under 5 JIT option sets, plus 6 more option sets on 4 seeds. There were 0 differences from -joff.
- PUC 5.3.6 with per-operator rounding equals -joff exactly.
- The generator catches each of five one-line sabotages of the fold in 60 of 60 seeds.
- Sanity floor on the prototype: t_rec seeds 1 and 2, counts seeds 3 and 4, and t_jit2 under 6 option sets all show 0 differences.

Two findings, neither a miscompile. (1) When the fold crosses a PHI and returns the int-typed loop index, the trace aborts with TYPEINS and is blacklisted: about 5.8x slower for `x = i | 0`-style loops. A one-line fix, measured, removes this at no cost. (2) The shipped JIT suites barely test the fold. t_rec, t_jit2 and the fuzzer miss all five sabotages, except for one t_rec counts recurrence that catches three of them.

I reproduced the claim from scratch in my own work dir and could not refute its core. It needs correcting, though: the gap is narrower than the title says, and it is a gap in the tests, not a VM defect.

BUILDS [M]
- I copied the b1 tree six times (the copied luajit.exe matched md5 0cd8b30da700) and applied the reviewer's sabotage.py, which I read first. Each sabotage is exactly one line, CRLF kept.

THE SABOTAGES ARE REAL, REACHABLE MISCOMPILES [M] (positive control, my own loops in scripts/wprobe.lua)
I compared the JIT against -joff, both with default options and with -O3 -Ohotloop=1 (runs/wprobe-2/SUMMARY.txt):
- The control has 0 differences on all 7 probes.
- w55: shr10 269 differing iterations, add1 539, add1b 538, shl32 546.
- shr: shr10 269, add1b 538, shl32 546.
- band: bandneg2 415.
- add0: add1b 538.

The -joff values equal PUC 5.3.6 with every result rounded to the nearest double (R(x)=x+0.0) on all six value probes (PUC-CHECK.txt), so the expected values are right.

Example (FIRST-DIFFS.txt): `local a=-i*1031-7; out=(a>>10)&0xffff` at i=58.
- a>>10 is 2^54-59, which rounds (ties to even) to 2^54-60.
- Expected 65476; the w55 and shr JIT give 65477.
- The defect site is lj_opt_fold.c:1219 for w55 and :1196 for shr, in the b1 build copy [S].

Two of my first probes were wrong and I replaced them:
- bandneg went out of range at i=512.
- add1 missed add0 because simplify_shiftk_andk rewrites (x&m)<<1 as BAND(ADD(x,x),2m), whose bound comes from the mask (runs/dump-add0/add0-dump.txt:25-26). This confirms the reviewer's note on that function.

SHIPPED SUITES ON THE SABOTAGES [M]
t_rec, seeds 1 and 2 (runs/suites-1/SUMMARY.txt):
- 0 for all five, with default options and with -Ohotloop=1.

t_rec counts, seed 3, run four times per build (rec-reruns-1/SUMMARY.txt):

Other suites:
- t_jit2 under six option sets: 0 for all five.
- t_sar: 0.
- bitfuzz, seed 1 x 1000 (the shipped default): PASS for all five, with all four controls behaving (runs/fuzz-1).

VERDICT PER SABOTAGE (shipped gates = t_rec in 4 runs, t_jit2, t_sar, fuzz at its default size)
- WIDTH55, band, add0: caught, each by a single t_rec counts-seed-3 recurrence. The design's "WIDTH55 [t_rec I]" (design.md:451) therefore holds, narrowly, and the title's implication that it does not is wrong for that arm.
- shr and shl0: caught by no shipped gate.

Beyond the defaults, from F6's campaign seeds:
- Fuzz seed 11 x 10000 catches w55 15, shr 15 (stable on a rerun) and band 8.
- Seed 12 x 10000 catches w55 1 and band 18.
- add0 and shl0: 0 at both seeds (fuzz-s11, fuzz-s11-rerun, fuzz-s12).
- shl0 was caught by nothing except my targeted loop.

NEW FINDING: the instrument behind the gap
t_jit2's rec-m54 is the test written for exactly this boundary ("bound 55: must NOT fold", t_jit2.lua:134-139), and it is vacuous [M]:
- Its mask literal 0x3fffffffffffff is read by LuaJIT's lexer (U9-A) as the double 2^54, a single bit.
- So x is 0 in all 400 iterations on the prototype; PUC 5.3.6 has 202 of 400 values at or above 2^53 (runs/m54-1).

t_rec's mask list M (t_rec.lua:26) has the same problem: 4 of its 9 masks do not act as masks on this VM (runs/literals-1):
- 0x3fffffffffffff reads as 2^54, and 0x7fffffffffffff as 2^55.
- 0x7fffffffffffffff and 0xfffffffffffff000 raise "no integer representation".

Its constant shift counts K (t_rec.lua:21) have no 10. Yet BSHR by 10 is the one leaf whose bound is exactly 55, and it is the shape the fuzzer caught at seed 11: `~((-2147483650) | (a << (-10)))`.

[I] A BAND with a non-negative double constant always gives a representable value, so its own round trip is exact. The bound-55 error shows only when an inexact bound-55 value (BSHR by 10, or a BOR/BXOR/BNOT over a bound-55 operand) reaches another bit operator.

CONCLUSION
The test gap is real and belongs to the prototype's shipped verification:
- Two one-line unsound changes to the width fold's bound rules escape every shipped gate.
- Three others are each held by one recurrence.
- The test meant to hold the boundary is vacuous because of literal rounding.

The headline overstates it: WIDTH55, the only width arm the design commits to, is caught by t_rec counts seed 3. The design does still mark it [I], and §12.1 asks for it to be shown caught.
